summary:
Martian: Mars Outpost Survival is a 2D educational survival and resource-management game designed for children aged 7–12. Players take on the role of a newly recruited astronaut tasked with rebuilding a damaged Mars outpost and keeping its crew alive for 15 days before a giant alien returns.

Players must manage essential resources such as Food, Power, Oxygen, Water, Shield and Health while repairing facilities, completing tasks and preparing for unpredictable Martian hazards. Every action requires careful planning, as limited Action Points force players to prioritise their decisions. On the final day, players must choose a strategy to confront the alien, with different endings depending on how they managed their resources.

The project addresses the challenge of making space exploration and decision-making engaging and accessible to younger audiences. By combining interactive gameplay with simplified survival mechanics inspired by real Mars exploration, it encourages critical thinking, resource management, problem-solving and an understanding of the challenges astronauts may face. Ultimately, it transforms complex scientific concepts into an enjoyable learning experience.
details:
Mars Outpost Survival is a free browser game for children aged 7–12. The player is a new astronaut sent to Mars after an alien attack wrecks the crew's outpost. They have 15 days to rebuild it, keep the crew alive, and get ready for the alien's return on Day 15.

How it works: Each day the player has a small number of Action Points (AP) to spend on tasks. They can repair the oxygen generator and water recycler, add solar panels, plant crops, build a radiation shelter, charge the shield, or visit the med bay. Every task shows what it will change before the player commits. Overnight the outpost uses up resources, and every few nights a hazard hits: solar flares, dust storms, meteor showers, oxygen leaks, dirty water, crop bugs and more. A crewmate warns the player the day before and hints at how to prepare. On Day 15 the player picks one plan to stop the alien: shield, food, power, or fight back. The plan only works if they built up the matching stat. A results screen then explains what happened and gives tips, and four different winning endings encourage replaying.

Benefits and impact: The game teaches resource management, planning, prioritising, and the trade-off between short-term fixes and long-term investment. It does this through real Mars survival needs: air, water, power, food, radiation and dust. Numbers always appear with icons and plain words, such as "15 / 50 Shield", so younger players learn to read data and make choices based on it. Failing is safe and teaches something: the "What happened?" screen explains the cause and suggests a better strategy.

Tools and technology: TypeScript (strict mode) and Vite, built as a static website hosted on GitHub Pages, so it runs on any desktop or tablet browser with nothing to install. The game rules are a pure-logic engine with automated tests (Vitest), plus a balance simulator that plays thousands of runs to check every ending is reachable. Randomness uses a seed, so any run can be replayed exactly when reporting bugs. Sound uses the Web Audio API, and progress saves in the browser.

Creativity: The setting is original, with its own characters (Commander Jasslyn, Jamie, the cat, and you!), a clickable illustrated outpost map, and a force-field dome that visibly grows as the player charges the shield. The art is hand-drawn and the music is chiptune.

Factors we considered: Accessibility for young players (large text, icons plus colour and never colour alone, short sentences, a skippable tutorial, a mute button). Fairness (the balance simulator confirms every ending can be won). Classroom use (it works on tablets, needs no accounts, and has quiet default volume). Original content only.
